Cautiously optimistic tone with explicit acknowledgment of risks. The Committee highlights strengthening activity and employment alongside “elevated” but mostly transitory inflation—language consistent with inflation-forecast targeting and average-inflation frameworks that tolerate temporary overshoots to anchor long-run expectations (Svensson and Woodford). The decision to keep rates at 0–0.25% while initiating a gradual taper of asset purchases aligns with New Keynesian guidance/forward guidance and QE practice (Woodford; Federal Reserve’s QE/FG literature), and recognizes cost-push/supply constraints emphasized in the NK Phillips curve and cost-channel studies (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Ravenna and Walsh). That said, uncertainty about shocks and the need to satisfy the Taylor principle over time (Clarida; Söderström) temper the overall tone.
